title: Integrate oncall feedback loop to tune tail sampling thresholds
creator: Priya Sharma
description: Add a lightweight operational feedback loop that lets oncall signals and incident annotations automatically tune per-route tail-sampling thresholds. Goal: reduce sustained tracing hotpath cost by lowering sample retention on low-value routes while preserving high-fidelity capture for real incidents and regression detection. This ticket covers design, prototyping, safety bounds, and a gradual rollout behind a feature flag.
acceptance_criteria: Auto-adjustments are confined by configurable min/max sampling rates per route and cannot disable sampling entirely
Incidents tagged as "tail_capture_needed" (or manual override) cause immediate bump to emergency retention that persists for a bounded time window
Observed p95 trace capture rate for routes that had historical regressions remains >= 90% after autoscaling thresholds are applied
End-to-end tests and canary show trace volume reduction >= 15% in synthetic high-throughput tests without increasing mean latency by >1ms
Feature flag + rollout controls present in Console with per-tenant opt-out and audit log entries
design_notes: We will consume two operational signals: incident state (open/severity) from PagerDuty and annotated alerts from Alertmanager/Grafana via a small webhook consumer
Map incident/alert tags to route selectors using the existing route-metadata registry (match on service_name, endpoint, customer_tier)
Adjustment algorithm: exponential decay smoothing + capped windowed overrides; parameters: alpha=0.4 (smoothing), min_rate=0.01, max_rate=1.0, emergency_hold=30m
Safety: changes only affect the local sampler's retention decision and never alter core request hotpath beyond a single atomic compare-and-swap to update in-memory thresholds
Telemetry: emit sampling_control.trace_updates metric with labels (route, old_rate, new_rate, reason) and maintain an audit log entry written to the tracing-control index
implementation_plan: 1) Add webhook microservice (trace-feedback-consumer) to ingest PagerDuty + Alertmanager webhooks and normalize signals
2) Extend route metadata API to accept operational tags and a 'dynamic_sampling_profile' field
3) Implement local sampler API to accept asynchronous threshold updates; updates must be lock-free and versioned
4) Add evaluation harness to replay past alert timelines against historical traces to validate capture fidelity
5) Build Console controls and feature flag to enable/disable per-org with rollout stages (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%)
6) Run staged rollout: internal-only -> partner tenants -> public with telemetry gating
tradeoffs_and_risks: Risk: noisy alerts could cause rapid oscillation; mitigated by smoothing and min dwell time on adjustments
Risk: operator error granting broad emergency_hold could temporarily spike cost; mitigated by RBAC and audit logs
Tradeoff: Prefer operational simplicity over optimal theoretical capture. We intentionally avoid heavy ML classifiers for now to keep runtime footprint small
Risk: False positives where incidents unrelated to user-facing regressions trigger emergency capture; require alert-tagging hygiene and runbook updates
metrics_and_success_signALS: trace_volume_total (sum) — expect -15% to -30% after stable rollout
sampling_control.updates_total by route and reason — monitor for noisy churn
tail_capture_precision@p95 — percent of true P95 regressions reconstructed from sampled traces (target >= 90%)
cost_per_token_trace — ensure per-token observation cost decreases or stays flat
oncall_feedback_rate — percent of incidents where oncall manual override was used (should be <5% after tuning)
rollout_plan: Feature flag off in prod by default
Internal canary on monitoring-team namespace for 48h; validate metrics and manual oncall feedback
Open to 10% of orgs for 72h, check sampling_control.updates_total and trace_volume reduction
If stable, increase to 50% for 1 week with tighter telemetry checks, then full rollout
Post-rollout 30-day watch with weekly retro and threshold tuning session with SREs and oncall leads
testing_plan: Unit tests for threshold update path and versioning semantics
Integration tests: simulate PagerDuty/Grafana webhooks and validate sampler applies bounded adjustments
Replay test: feed historical alert timeline and trace corpus to evaluation harness and calculate tail_capture_precision
Load test: synthetic QPS to verify update path is lock-free and does not add >0.5ms median overhead
Chaos test: ensure emergency_hold expiry and manual rollback operate as expected
